articles.title: "I treat every game like it's the last": Kelly Stafford's emotional approach to Matthew Stafford's 18th NFL season reveals what has changed for her
articles.summary: Kelly Stafford has watched her husband play professional football for nearly two decades.
articles.body: Kelly Stafford has watched her husband play professional football for nearly two decades. She has stood on sidelines, packed up homes, raised four daughters largely on her own during seasons, and cheered through a Super Bowl. Eighteen years in, something has shifted. Not the love for the game, but the awareness of how little time may be left. Speaking to PEOPLE shortly after the Rams' opening loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Australia on September 10, Kelly was candid about the mindset she is carrying into the 2026 season."Every season now I will say I'm treating it like the last," she said. "It's been 18 years now. It's been a wild, wild ride."Why is Kelly Stafford treating Matthew's 18th NFL season like it could be his last?Matthew Stafford, 38, was the Detroit Lions' first overall pick back in 2009. He spent 12 seasons in Detroit before the trade to Los Angeles in 2021, where he wasted no time -- winning a Super Bowl in his very first year with the Rams. The football resume is almost complete. Now, with four daughters old enough to understand what their father actually does for a living, the stakes feel different.Kelly, 37, says that shift with the girls has made this season feel more precious than any before. "Now that all of my girls understand football and what their dad does -- that is truly special, 'cause a lot of guys don't get to this point where their kids are this old," she told PEOPLE.Twins Sawyer and Chandler are nine. Hunter is eight. Tyler is six. They show up to games in spirited outfits, sprint to their dad before kickoff, and have apparently started lobbying against retirement. "They're the ones that are like, 'Daddy, you can't not play. What do you mean? You have to play,'" Kelly laughed.What does Kelly Stafford say about attending Rams games with her daughters this season?Kelly's approach this year is almost deliberate in its mindfulness. She is mentally marking firsts and lasts -- last time in a particular stadium, last time against a certain team -- because she genuinely does not know when the final game will come."Who knows if it is, 'cause I never know," she admitted. "I just love watching him play. I really do. It's one of my favorite things in life -- to watch him do what he loves."The sideline moments, she says, fill something in her that she is already bracing to lose. "The feeling of taking the girls to the game and watching their dad run over -- that fills my soul with so much joy. I'm going to completely miss it when it's gone so much, but I also have to prepare for that moment."For now, she is not rushing that preparation. articles.title: Caleb Williams Gets Discouraging Injury Update Before Bears-Eagles Game
articles.summary: Caleb Williams received a discouraging injury update before the Bears-Eagles game, putting the Chicago quarterback’s status in focus. The post Caleb Williams...
articles.body:
Caleb Williams will not play Monday night against the Philadelphia Eagles , according to NFL Network 's Ian Rapoport, meaning that the Chicago Bears will fall back on their third option quarterback, Case Keenum , to start Week 3.

The update from the longtime NFL insider should put an end to days of hedging from Chicago 's coaching staff and thrusts 38-year-old Keenum into his first regular-season start since 2023, with an offense built around Williams' agile legs.

Williams left Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings in the fourth quarter, pulling up lame on a non-contact scramble near the goal line with Chicago trailing, according to NFL.com . He was carted off, then later spotted walking through the locker room under his own power, favoring the leg only slightly.

All times Eastern. Home games at Soldier Field, Chicago, IL. Bye in Week 10. Week 18 is a flex game — date and broadcast TBD.

Williams had thrown for 138 yards and an interception on 15 of 26 passing, adding 42 rushing yards, before handing the offense to backup Tyson Bagent .

Monday's MRI turned up no tear, and coach Ben Johnson called the results somewhat encouraging, cautioning Williams would likely miss time. By Thursday, the team had ruled him out of practice entirely, and Rapoport's own tone had shifted from unlikely to play earlier in the week to a flat no.

Johnson has praised Williams' recovery pace throughout the week, saying the quarterback is "a little bit different than your average human being" as a healer and confirming he has stayed involved in walk-throughs and meetings .

Thursday's session amounted to an estimation with the Bears off Thursday ahead of Monday night, but both Williams and Bagent were listed as non-participants on the injury report , according to the Chicago Tribune .

Keenum, 38, is the last man standing in Chicago's quarterback room after Bagent entered the NFL's concussion protocol Tuesday following a hit from Minnesota linebacker Andrew Van Ginkel , according to ABC7 Chicago 's Courtney Cronin.

"I feel very prepared. It's what I do every week. It's what I've done for a long time. If my name's called, I'm excited to be out there," Keenum said as quoted by ABC7 Chicago .

Keenum took every rep with the first-team offense Wednesday while undrafted rookie Miller Moss ran the scout-team offense, and the Bears do not plan to sign a fourth quarterback, according to the same report. Keenum, a 15-year veteran, has made 66 career starts for 15,175 yards and 79 touchdowns but has not thrown a regular-season pass since 2023 with Houston , though he owns a 3-0 record as a starter against Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio.

Hamstring strains like Williams' typically cost two to four weeks, and the Bears have shown no urgency to rush him back even as Johnson insists the quarterback heals faster than most. Friday's practice, the team's first real session of the week, will offer the clearest read yet on whether the absence stretches beyond Week 3.

articles.title: Falcons Beat Packers, Box Score Stats, Highlights for Bijan, Penix, London, Jordan Love, Top Players
articles.summary: The Atlanta Falcons pulled off an upset victory over the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night, winning by the final score of 35-14 at Lambeau Field.
articles.body:
The Atlanta Falcons pulled off an upset victory over the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night, winning by the final score of 35-14 at Lambeau Field.

Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. made his season debut after recovering from a torn ACL , playing his first game since Nov. 2025.

Atlanta was able to emerge victorious after entering the contest as 4.5-point underdogs, according to FanDuel Sportsbook .

Bijan Robinson, Drake London and Matthew Golden were among the standout fantasy football performers in the game.

With the win, Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski improved to 6-0 in Thursday night games.

Penix's return didn't start on a high note, as he was picked off by Packers safety Xavier McKinney on Atlanta's opening drive.

Both teams traded punts before the Packers entered the end zone first, as Jordan Love connected with Christian Watson for a short touchdown.

The Falcons didn't take long to respond, immediately going on an 85-yard drive that ended with a three-yard touchdown run by Robinson.

Green Bay's running backs struggled to match his production, amassing a mere 17 yards on the ground as a team. The Packers also averaged just 1.9 yards per carry.

Atlanta eventually took its first lead of the night with a field goal in the second quarter, while Green Bay's game-tying field goal attempt was later blocked.

The Falcons' defense stifled the Packers throughout the first half, forcing another Green Bay punt before Penix found Austin Hooper for a five-yard score.

The Packers appeared to be gaining momentum to start the third quarter, driving to the Falcons' seven-yard line. Green Bay came up empty-handed after failing to convert on fourth down, though.

Atlanta extended its advantage to 17 points on the team's next possession, as Brian Robinson Jr. picked up a seven-yard rushing touchdown of his own.

The Packers attempted to mount a late comeback after Love hit Matthew Golden for a 15-yard touchdown, but the Falcons eventually put the game out of reach with a 67-yard drive that was capped off by Bijan's second score of the night.

Atlanta was able to routinely move the ball down the field, finishing with 498 total yards while averaging 7.5 yards per play. The Falcons picked up 25 first downs across 11 drives.

The Packers couldn't keep up, converting just six of their 15 opportunities on third down.

Atlanta and Green Bay both sit at 1-2 following Thursday's result.

Desperation begins early in an NFL season. A 0-3 start makes it nearly impossible to make the postseason, though the Houston Texans did so last season. Prior to the Texans, only six other teams in the modern era accomplished the same goal. Entering Week 3, eight teams faced the possibility of an 0-3 start, starting with the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday Night Football . For others, a season can be over much sooner than anyone expects.

Bleacher Report NFL analysts Brent Sobleski , Kris Knox , and Moe Moton will follow all of the action to break down each contest, provide takeaways and ask the most pressing questions.

Michael Penix Jr.'s Growing Confidence Provides Hope For Atlanta Falcons

The Atlanta Falcons already featured immense offensive talent at numerous spots. The quarterback position continued to hold back the team, though. Michael Penix Jr.s' performance Thursday against Green Bay Packers was quite promising after significant disappointment earlier in his career.

Penix started slowly during his first start after coming back from a torn ACL, including a poor interception on the opening drive where safety Xavier McKinney read the quarterback's eyes and easily drove on the pass for the turnover. From there, the 2024 eighth overall draft pick benefited greatly from Bijan Robinson running wild, offensive coordinator Tommy Rees giving the quarterback simple reasons and plenty of quick-hitters and manufactured touches to build the 26-year-old's confidence.

By the end of the game, Penix finished the contest with 256 passing and a touchdown. He also completed 72 percent of his passes.

The quarterback's performance is exactly what Atlanta needed to try and build something positive. It's a significant turn of events considering the Falcons wanted to enter this season with Tua Tagovailoa as their QB1.

Spoiler Alert: Bijan Robinson Continues to Run Wild

Robinson is arguably the game's best running back. The Packers won't argue after Thursday's performance.

Green Bay knew it had to slow the Falcons' lead back and failed spectacularly when trying to do so. Robinson's 29 carries became a new career-high, while he finished two short of doing the same with 194 rushing yards.

The 24-year-old ball-carrier sliced through Green Bay's defense, scored twice and served as a big-play threat even though Penix wasn't comfortable early and the Packers could key on Atlanta's run game—which showed how dynamic he really is.

Can Green Bay Do Anything To Improve Its Run Game? The Packers entered Thursday's contest with the league's worst rushing offense. Green Bay's latest performance only made matters worse. Matt LaFleur's unit had been averaging 64.5 rushing yards per game. The Packers managed a measly 17 yards against the Falcons. MarShawn Lloyd led the team. He produced 11 yards on four carries. With Josh Jacobs' on the commissioner's exempt list with a potential league suspension forthcoming, general manager Brian Gutekunst must look at alternatives. Remaining free agents aren't promising. A potential trade could happen. The New Orleans Saints' Alvin Kamara may be the biggest name on the trade block. Of course, the offensive line could help matters, but that doesn't seem likely. Packers' O-Line Is Making Life Miserable for QB Jordan Love Four-fifths of Green Bay's front five is unproven and it shows. Jacob Monk moved from center to right guard, and he's a full-time starter for the first time in the NFL career. Anthony Belton took over at right tackle after Zach Bako-Bewele suffered a season-ending knee injury. Rookie Jager Burton moved into left guard for the injured Aaron Banks. Plus, Jordan Morgan may be a former first-round pick, but this season is his first as the squad's left tackle. As a result, Green Bay can't run the ball, and Love isn't comfortable in the pocket. While the Falcons sacked Love only once, Atlanta hit him on 12 different occasions and applied consistent pressure. An offense can't do much if its offensive line isn't solid, and Green Bay is a prime example.

Once the weekend's games begin, the haves and have nots can be established rather quickly.

The Buffalo Bills can make a disappointing start even more devastating for the Los Angeles Chargers. The Kansas City Chiefs once again look like a Super Bowl contender, and Andy Reid's squad is set to face the NFL's least talented team in the Miami Dolphins. articles.title: Bijan Robinson runs roughshod over the Packers as the Falcons breeze to a 35-14 victory
articles.summary: Robinson rushed for 194 yards and two touchdowns as Atlanta capitalized on the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr.
articles.body: Bijan Robinson rushed for 194 yards and two touchdowns as the Atlanta Falcons capitalized on the return of quarterback Michael Penix Jr. and trounced the punchless Green Bay Packers 35-14 on Thursday night. Atlanta (1-2) erased an early 7-0 deficit by scoring 27 straight points to take control amid a chorus of boos at Lambeau Field. The Falcons outrushed the Packers 242 yards to 17. Green Bay (1-2) lost a home opener for the first time since falling 30-22 to the San Francisco 49ers in 2012. The Packers had won 13 straight home openers from 2013 to 2025 to share the NFL record with the Miami Dolphins, who also won 13 in a row from 1976 to 1988. Penix went 18 of 25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and an interception in his first action since tearing the ACL in his left knee during a loss to Carolina on Nov. 16. Atlanta (1-2) had struggled to produce any offense whatsoever with Cooper Rush starting at quarterback the first two weeks of the season. That wasn’t a problem Thursday. Robinson and Drake London became the first teammates to each compile at least 150 yards from scrimmage against the Packers at Lambeau Field. London caught nine passes for 194 yards. Green Bay’s Jordan Love went 28 of 53 for 312 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson combined for 17 yards on eight carries. Love was working behind an offensive line missing left guard Aaron Banks and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, who tore his patellar tendon Sunday and will miss the rest of the season. Banks was dealing with a toe injury. Jager Burton, a rookie fifth-round pick from Kentucky, made his first career start at left guard, and 2025 second-round selection Anthony Belton started at right tackle. The lack of discipline that hindered Green Bay in its first two games cropped up again Thursday. Green Bay led 7-0 and had forced an apparent third-and-11 incompletion late in the first quarter when Brenton Cox Jr. was called for roughing the passer. Robinson delivered a 55-yard carry on the next play to set up his own 3-yard touchdown run. The Packers had committed an NFL-high 26 penalties through the first two weeks of the season. Robinson’s long run allowed Atlanta to take a snap inside an opponent’s 20-yard line for the first time this season. Atlanta had been the first team since the 2008 Rams not to run any plays in the red zone through the first two weeks of a season. Atlanta dominated the rest of the first half and led 17-7 at the break. Nick Folk put Atlanta ahead by hitting a 44-yard field goal with 4:48 left in the second quarter. After Atlanta’s Zach Harrison blocked Trey Smack’s 47-yard field-goal attempt, Penix threw a 5-yard touchdown pass to Austin Hooper on third-and-goal with 59 seconds left in the half. Green Bay wasted a red-zone opportunity on its first drive of the second half when Love couldn’t connect with Christian Watson in the end zone on fourth-and-1 from the 7. Atlanta extended the lead to 24-7 on its next possession, as Brian Robinson’s 7-yard touchdown run capped a 10-play, 92-yard drive. Folk added a 31-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter before Love threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden with 8:18 remaining. Robinson capped the scoring with a 2-yard TD.

articles.title: Packers' shocking blowout loss to Falcons should put coach Matt LaFleur on the hot seat
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers fell to 1-2 as Matt LaFleur's hot seat questions intensify after a blowout home loss to the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night.
articles.body: The Green Bay Packers finally opened Lambeau Field for the first time this regular season, where they hoped to make it 14 straight home openers where they’ve come away with a victory on Thursday night against a struggling Atlanta Falcons team. Instead, the Packers were blown out by an 0-2 team on their home turf, and now a big question arises. Should head coach Matt LaFleur be on the hot seat? CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE LaFleur signed a multi-year contract extension at the beginning of this year, which wasn’t considered a "prove-it deal," per ESPN. But what happened in this 35-14 loss certainly warms his seat as the Packers fall to 1-2 to start the year. It wasn’t just this performance, either. In Week 1, a second-half collapse resulted in a Vikings victory to open the season. Then, the Packers were close to falling to the New York Jets on the road in a game they were heavily favored. It took overtime in rainy conditions to escape New Jersey with a 20-17 win. As for Thursday night’s performance, it was more of the same that was seen in the first two weeks: a lack of diversity between the run and pass games, poor offensive line play and quarterback Jordan Love not being able to handle the pressure in his pocket. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The sold-out Lambeau Field crowd was raining down boos and jeers from the stands throughout this contest, as Love and his receivers couldn’t get on the same page, drives stalled and the Falcons started to find their offensive spark now that Michael Penix Jr. was finally healthy enough to play. Oh, and Bijan Robinson once again proved why he is one of those rare NFL talents with his ability to totally take over a game when he has the ball in his hands. Before we get to the Falcons’ positives in this game, back to LaFleur’s situation in Green Bay. Since last year, including the Wild Card Round, the Packers are just 1-7 in their last eight contests. As the fan base collectively shakes their heads at the start of this season, and audibly shows their frustration at the first home game of the season, could the thought of keeping sustainability at the head coach position change in Green Bay? LaFleur entered his eighth season with the Packers this year, and he is the only active head coach that has been with his team that long and not reached the Super Bowl. Yes, it’s still early in the season, but just food for thought. On the other sideline, there were tons of smiles, and none more infectious than that of Robinson, who finished the game with 194 rushing yards and two touchdowns. All week long, the Packers preached stopping Robinson, understanding that’s exactly what happened in Weeks 1 and 2, when the Falcons struggled to get anything going on offense. Well, Robinson torched this Packers defense with chunk runs, including a 55-yarder, and that also made life easier for Penix’s return under center. The Falcons’ signal caller, whom they wished could’ve been healthy to start the year but hadn’t been fully recovered from his torn ACL in 2025, found his rhythm after opening the game with an interception on Atlanta’s first drive. The Falcons drew up quick passing plays for Penix to get going, and once the Packers had to respect Robinson’s running ability, play-action passes were Penix’s bread and butter. Most of them went to Drake London, who also had his breakout game of the season. Like Robinson, he also had 194 yards, though through nine receptions, including a 68-yard catch-and-run that sealed the deal in the fourth quarter for the Falcons. He may not have had a touchdown, but this was the performance Penix needed after not finding anything with Cooper Rush in the first two games of the year. But for the Packers, tough questions need to be asked already this year because it seems to be picking up where it left off in the worst ways possible.

articles.title: These NFL rookies are outperforming their draft slots. One of them wasn't even drafted
articles.summary: Here are the players having outsized roles during their inaugural campaigns who were picked 33rd and beyond in the NFL Draft.
articles.body:
What makes the NFL and its draft so interesting — other than seeing the next step for college heroes — is that rookies can typically make immediate and tangible impacts on a team's fortunes for the upcoming season. And it's not just first-rounders, either.

Through two weeks of this NFL season, there are a lot of interesting rookies getting playing time and important roles for their teams. I wanted to highlight a crop of them, which actually was hard for me to pare down. This is carryover from a broader discussion about this year's draft class: the projected first-rounders were underwhelming, but there was a lot of depth and potential with the players slated to go in the second round and beyond.

Here are the players having outsized roles during their inaugural campaigns that were picked 33rd and beyond:

Jaishawn Barham , LB, Cowboys, pick No. 92

After a strong preseason and a Week 1 game that seemed to have his head spinning , the Cowboys slapped the green dot on Barham in Week 2 and he proceeded to fly around and impact the game against the Commanders.

Barham still has coverage stuff to clean up and does his best work going forward in the run game and as a blitzer (where his edge background from college shows up), but it was an encouraging performance seeing him not only make plays against the run, but force a fumble on a screen, too.

The Cowboys' defense is still a major work in progress , but Barham has already put together more positive plays in the middle than anybody else suiting up for Dallas last year.

Now, if they could only get off the field on third down …

Also, speaking of linebackers, Josiah Trotter (pick No. 46) has had moments for the Buccaneers, including a Week 1 pick 6. There has been some botches in the Bucs' defense overall, but he's very young and his downhill style should fit well in Todd Bowles' preferred chaos as he gets more comfortable.

Hezekiah Masses, CB, Raiders, pick No. 175

Not a player I thought I'd be writing about so early this season! But Masses already has multiple interceptions in his young career, along with other big plays against the run.

It's not just the turnovers he's forced. Masses has already put out good film where he stays sticky in one-on-one situations with wide receivers.

Now, the Dolphins and the sloppy Chargers aren't exactly world-beaters, and Masses will have a much stiffer challenge this week with Saints receivers Chris Olave and even Devaughn Vele , who is Mr. Reliable for Tyler Shough . But so far he looks like a feisty cornerback willing to play the run. That's an archetype that's always an enjoyable watch.

Austin Barber, OG, Browns, pick No. 86 Denzel Boston, WR, Browns, pick No. 39

Looks like Browns general manager Andrew Berry's hot streak in the draft continues! Austin Barber, who played tackle at Florida, was kicked inside during preseason to right guard. And all he has done since is stack up strong film, including not allowing a single pressure in Week 2 on 36 pass-blocking snaps against the Buccaneers.

Denzel Boston caught a long touchdown in the midst of a Week 1 blowout loss against the Jaguars, but then kept the good times rolling in Week 2. He's on the field almost every snap for the Browns' offense and has already shown off his body control and strong hands on the outside. He also has the ability to pick up yards after the catch when he does work over the middle. Boston looks like a true X who can win in isolated situations, which he's shown through two weeks and in the preseason. He has topped 20 mph multiple times this season (per NextGenStats), easing concerns about his long speed and ability to separate. Boston doesn't look just like a keeper, he looks like a guy you can build a passing game around.

Also, a shoutout to two more Day 2 wide receivers in the Commanders' Antonio Williams (pick No. 71) and Malachi Fields for the Giants (pick No. 74). Williams looks like a slot demon with some real juice to threaten defenses vertically and Fields is already one of the better blocking receivers in the NFL right now. He has only 55 receiving yards so far, but his role might expand quickly with Malik Nabers hurt again and Jameis Winston throwing balls up like it's a game of 500. Also, keep an eye on Ted Hurst (pick No. 84) for the Buccaneers. He has been thrust into a role early as the Bucs try to find an outside option.

One of the most unexpected names on this list! It's not because Benson lacks talent — he clearly has it, and he put together a strong preseason at guard . But "good preseason tape at right guard" is way different than "starting at left tackle in Week 1." And Benson has more than held his own on the blindside and been a part of this more explosive Chiefs offense that is pounding it in the run game and allowing Patrick Mahomes to party like it's 2021 with the deep ball.

Hunter's appeal in college was in his flashes. I loved his quick feet but had concerns about how much he tried to backdoor blocks despite weighing over 315 pounds and not being a tip-top athlete. Well, it turns out that when asked to hold down at the point of attack, he can use that size and strength to affect the run!

Hunter plays a role that might not always show up in the box score, but he is a great type of running mate to pair with Derrick Brown . It's been an encouraging showing for him early in his career. His Panthers teammate Will Lee III (pick No. 129) has had a couple of moments in coverage, too. And Hunter's college teammate (at least for one year at Texas Tech) Skyler Gill-Howard (pick No. 205) has been an interesting, undersized gap shooter for the Lions.

A couple of more defensive tackles have shown up early too. Gracen Halton (pick No. 107) was almost needed to play well for the 49ers to hold up against the run this year. He's not only brought some stoutness to clear the way for Fred Warner to do his thing, but real explosiveness to make tackles.

Domonique Orange (pick No. 82) has done the same for the Vikings, who tried to inject some youth into their front with Big Citrus and their first-round pick Caleb Banks. While Banks has shown off his talent, and his at times maddening inconsistency, Orange has been much more steady to start his career and fits this Vikings defense, with its constant movement up front, perfectly.

Pick a Dolphins rookie, cause they needed it!

Caleb Douglas (pick No. 75) at the very least looks the part. He's a big, strong athlete who eats up ground with his strides. He has shown great feel for using his size. He even had impressive snaps from the slot, throwing defenders off before breaking and coming down with the football against Taron Johnson in Week 1, one top of his snaps as an isolated outside receiver. Jacob Rodriguez (No. 43) has been a tackling machine, and one of two rookies in the league to wear the defensive green dot. And even Michael Taaffe (No. 158) has shown off range as a deep safety, and I like his feel for playing high-lows when asked to play as a quarters safety.

There's plenty of playing time to go around in Miami , and these three have all shown flashes and even sustained play that makes me want to keep peeking at this Dolphins team that is purely playing for their future anyway. Just as long as they don't play the 49ers, Brock Purdy and Kyle Shanahan every week.

Here's another young linebacker filling up the box score. Hill is a great athlete who can be slow to react at times in diagnosing what's happening in front of him. The game looked like it slowed down a bit for him in Week 2 against the Eagles, and he constantly gets himself around the ball. Hopefully the slew of tackles starts turning into something more impactful, but it's encouraging that what I thought would be a sideline-to-sideline player has held up OK early when working in the box.

And speaking of Titans: Fernando Carmona, the 142nd overall draft pick, has been at the very least playable at guard. His best work is in the run game, so even if he had some losses in pass protection over the first two weeks, it's still encouraging he's been able to hold up.

These two might not have box score numbers, but their production might start showing up more as the season goes along.

Cashius Howell, Edge, Bengals (pick No. 41) Dani Dennis-Sutton , Edge, Packers (pick No. 120)

Two complete opposite ends of the spectrum in terms of build here. Howell is a designated pass rusher type who hasn't made a blip in the box score. But his underlying numbers and flashes on film indicate it's only a matter of time before he starts getting home. Howell has already racked up nine pressures and a 20.5% pressure rate, ranking second and third among rookies, respectively, according to Next Gen Stats.

(He should have gotten credited with a sack on the play embedded below).

The player to top the leaderboard for pressure rate among rookies entering Thursday? Dani Dennis-Sutton. A fourth-round selection, Dennis-Sutton has been a key contributor to coordinator Jonathan Gannon's Packers defense — a group trying to keep their heads above water until Micah Parsons returns. Instead, Dennis-Sutton and Lukas Van Ness , in the midst of a breakout season, and even personal favorite Karl Brooks , have been taking it to offensive lines whether rushing four or blitzing on passing downs.

7 other notable rookies, including the man who caught first TD in 2026 NFL season

The Bears' defense has been ( wavers hand) so far, but Malik Muhammad (pick No. 124) has had some moments, even when some of his veteran teammates have been faltering around him. A dynamic slot player is important in Dennis Allen's defense, and Muhammad holding it down while Kyler Gordon is out (again) is at least one encouraging aspect of this defense.

Patriots tight end Eli Raridon (pick No. 95) opened up the NFL season with the first touchdown of the year in Week 1. He's already asked to be the in-line blocker on run plays, and the Patriots even attempted to dial up shot plays to him in Week 2. I'm bullish on Raridon and think he can end up as a strong starter who can stay on the field every down sooner than later. He even has over 2 yards per route run. And yes, I know. Small sample size.

And speaking of Patriots rookies, Gabe Jacas (pick No. 55) keeps showing up for New England 's defense. Jacas has strong hands, but he's also shown off some quickness after the snap, and he's not only holding up at the point of attack, but impacting games with big plays for the defense, too.

Jaguars offensive guard Emmanuel Pregnon (pick No. 88) had a strong start in Week 1, especially in the run game, before coming back down to Earth a bit going against Zach Allen in Week 2. Still, his double-teams with Anton Harrison are appointment viewing, and him just even being an average starter as a rookie will help the Jaguars' offense stay explosive on the ground and through the air as he helps shore up their offensive line.

Let's round it out with a few running backs. Kenneth Walker has exploded out of the gates for the Chiefs' running game, but Emmett Johnson (pick No. 161) has kept the juice flowing when he's on the field. Keeping Walker fresh is important for the Chiefs to keep rolling on the ground this year, and Johnson holding his own whenever he's out there is a really good sign for this KC offense maintaining its start.

Same with Kaelon Black (pick No. 90) for the 49ers. With Christian McCaffrey coming off a heavy workload last season, having another running back who has a great feel and vision on zone runs, plus ability as a pass protector, is a welcome addition to the 49ers' backfield that has been rotating players behind the dynamic CMC for years. Black looks like he can maintain efficiency in this offense as a runner and help out in other ways with his pass protection.

Speaking of protection, how about CJ Donaldson , an undrafted player for the Saints, getting the important passing down reps for New Orleans (he has only 4 rushing yards) even with veterans Travis Etienne and Alvin Kamara , with their combined $16 million salary cap hit this year, on the roster. That might speak more negatively about Etienne and Kamara, players who have struggled in protection over the past few years, but it's still notable that Donaldson is getting these snaps.

Top takeaways from Thursday Night Football

articles.title: NFL: Green Bay Packers booed in Atlanta Falcons loss as Bijan Robinson and Drake London star
articles.summary: Bijan Robinson and Drake London combined for 407 total yards of offense as the Atlanta Falcons cruised past the Green Bay Packers following the return of starting quarterback Michael Penix Jr from injury; Week Three in the NFL continues Sunday, live on Sky Sports from 5.30pm
articles.body:
Atlanta (1-2) erased an early 7-0 deficit by scoring 27 straight points to take control amid a chorus of boos at Lambeau Field. The Falcons outrushed the Packers 242 yards to 17.

Green Bay (1-2) lost a home opener for the first time since falling 30-22 to the San Francisco 49ers in 2012. The Packers had won 13 straight home openers from 2013-25 to share the NFL record with the Miami Dolphins, who also won 13 in a row from 1976-88.

Penix went 18 of 25 for 256 yards with one touchdown and an interception in his first action since tearing the ACL in his left knee during a loss to Carolina on November 16. Atlanta (1-2) had struggled to produce any offense whatsoever with Cooper Rush starting at quarterback the first two weeks of the season.

Passing: Michael Penix Jr, 18/25, 256 yards, 1 TD, 1 INT

Rushing: Bijan Robinson, 29 carries, 194 yards, 2 TDs

Receiving: Drake London, 9 carries, 194 yards

Passing: Jordan Love, 28/53, 312 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT

Rushing: MarShawn Lloyd, 4 carries, 11 yards

Receiving: Matthew Golden, 5 catches, 100 yards, 1 TD

Robinson and Drake London became the first team-mates to each compile at least 150 yards from scrimmage against the Packers at Lambeau Field. London caught nine passes for 194 yards.

Green Bay's Jordan Love went 28 of 53 for 312 yards with two touchdowns and an interception. MarShawn Lloyd and Kaleb Johnson combined for 17 yards on eight carries.

Love was working behind an offensive line missing left guard Aaron Banks and right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele, who tore his patellar tendon Sunday and will miss the rest of the season. Banks was dealing with a toe injury.

Jager Burton, a rookie fifth-round pick from Kentucky, made his first career start at left guard, and 2025 second-round selection Anthony Belton started at right tackle.

The lack of discipline that hindered Green Bay in its first two games cropped up again Thursday.

Green Bay led 7-0 and had forced an apparent third-and-11 incompletion late in the first quarter when Brenton Cox Jr. was called for roughing the passer. Robinson delivered a 55-yard carry on the next play to set up his own 3-yard touchdown run.

The Packers had committed an NFL-high 26 penalties through the first two weeks of the season.

Robinson's long run allowed Atlanta to take a snap inside an opponent's 20-yard line for the first time this season. Atlanta had been the first team since the 2008 Rams not to run any plays in the red zone through the first two weeks of a season.

Atlanta dominated the rest of the first half and led 17-7 at the break.

Nick Folk put Atlanta ahead by hitting a 44-yard field goal with 4:48 left in the second quarter. After Atlanta's Zach Harrison blocked Trey Smack's 47-yard field-goal attempt, Penix threw a five-yard touchdown pass to Austin Hooper on third-and-goal with 59 seconds left in the half.

Green Bay wasted a red-zone opportunity on its first drive of the second half when Love couldn't connect with Christian Watson in the end zone on fourth-and-one from the seven Atlanta extended the lead to 24-7 on its next possession, as Brian Robinson's seven-yard touchdown run capped a 10-play, 92-yard drive.

Folk added a 31-yard field goal early in the fourth quarter before Love threw a 15-yard touchdown pass to Matthew Golden with 8:18 remaining. Bijan Robinson capped the scoring with a two-yard TD.

articles.title: NFL: Green Bay Packers booed during 'butt-whooping' at home to Atlanta Falcons
articles.summary: The Green Bay Packers' head coach Matt LaFleur says his team got a "butt-whooping" as they lost 35-14 at home to the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers' head coach Matt LaFleur said his team got a "butt-whooping" as they lost 35-14 at home to the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday.

The Packers were booed by their own fans as they were well beaten by a Falcons team that lost 34-3 at home to the Carolina Panthers on Sunday.

Although a depleted Green Bay opened the scoring at Lambeau Field, the Falcons hit back with 27 unanswered points.

Their 498 yards on offence included 242 rushing yards, while Green Bay's total 328 yards featured just 17 from nine carries.

"They had 500 yards of offence, we had whatever it was - it was a butt-whooping," said LaFleur.

"I'm not going to put it on one thing. We definitely have to respond better but that was at least a three-quarter butt-whooping right there."

The Falcons' offence struggled as they lost their first two games of the NFL season but quarterback Michael Penix Jr's return from knee surgery helped them bounce back.

Running back Bijan Robinson rushed for two touchdowns and 194 yards, and added 19 receiving yards, while Drake London racked up 194 receiving yards from just nine catches.

The Packers were already without defensive star Micah Parsons and running back Josh Jacobs but lost two offensive linemen to injury in last week's win at the New York Jets.

Although the hosts took the lead through a Christian Watson touchdown, the Falcons then took charge with Bijan Robinson, Austin Hooper and Brian Robinson Jr all getting into the endzone while Nick Folk added two field goals.

Matthew Golden's touchdown stopped the rot for the Packers but Bijan Robinson claimed his second score late on to seal an emphatic win for the Falcons.

Both teams now have a 1-2 record, with Green Bay visiting Tampa Bay next Sunday while Atlanta travel to divisional rivals New Orleans a week on Monday.

articles.title: Bills Called Top Trade Destination for Struggling Former No. 4 Overall Pick
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills called top traded destination for struggling former No. 4 overall pick. The post Bills Called Top Trade Destination for Struggling Former No. 4...
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills might just be 1 player away from having the NFL's most dynamic offense — and the only position that lift could possibly come at is wide receiver.

If that happens in 2026, it would probably have to be via trade, and Bleacher Report's Moe Moton called the Bills the NFL's top trade destination for struggling Arizona Cardinals wide receiver and 2024 No. 2 overall pick Marvin Harrison Jr.

"(GM) Brandon Beane may be willing to offer the best trade package for Harrison, a 24-year-old receiver who hasn't reached his peak," Moton wrote. "The Bills can exercise the fifth-year option on his rookie deal to keep him under team control for two more years while they figure out where he fits in their offense. Unless Keon Coleman breaks out this year, Harrison can be the new featured target on the perimeter opposite Moore, with Shakir in the slot. It would be a well-rounded group of receivers with Harrison as the potential long-term centerpiece."

Harrison Jr. Entered NFL With Massive Fanfare

Few wide receiver prospects have entered the NFL with as much fanfare as the 6-foot-3, 205-pound Harrison Jr., the son of Pro Football Hall of Fame wide receiver Marvin Harrison.

Selected No. 4 overall by the Cardinals in the 2024 NFL Draft out of Ohio State, the red flags started to pop up during his rookie season. On the surface, he had a respectable season with 62 receptions for 885 yards and 8 touchdowns — until you also consider he did so with an incredible 116 targets.

While the Cardinals went 8-9 in 2024, they dropped to 3-14 in 2025. Harrison finished with 41 receptions for 608 yards and 4 touchdowns in 12 games and battled a whole smorgasbord of injuries — a concussion in Week 6, an appendectomy kept him out 2 games, a heel injury in Week 13, and a foot injury in Week 17 before the Cardinals finally placed him on season-ending injured reserve.

Struggles Have Continued Into 2026 Regular Season

Through 2 games in 2026, Harrison Jr. has just 1 reception for 33 yards.

Combined with a preseason in which it seemed like a new viral clip of Harrison Jr. dropping a pass at practice went viral every week, it's been a rough stretch for a player NFL Draft analyst Lance Zierlein called a "pedigree prospect and a Day 1 starter with high-end production expected" in his pre-draft evaluation.

"It's the social media era," Harrison told AzCardinals.com's Darren Urban . "You see everything. I'm not going to sit here and say I don't see nothing. You get told to block out the noise and not pay attention to it. That's part of it. Everyone is entitled to their own opinions. I'm just going to continue to worry about my team, my process."

articles.title: Giants news: Jaxson Dart's devastating injury draws strong Brian Daboll reaction
articles.summary: The New York Giants suffered a crushing blow to their 2026 NFL campaign when starting quarterback Jaxson Dart sustained a season-ending knee injury during a...
articles.body:
The New York Giants suffered a crushing blow to their 2026 NFL campaign when starting quarterback Jaxson Dart sustained a season-ending knee injury during a 28-6 loss against the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium.

The devastating news resonated across the league, particularly for former Giants head coach Brian Daboll , who now serves as the offensive coordinator for the Tennessee Titans . Daboll, who drafted Dart in the first round of the 2025 NFL Draft, shared a heartfelt response when reporters asked about his former signal-caller.

"Yeah that's tough, it's always tough, I have a very good relationship with him, obviously devastated with what happened," Daboll said. "…It was a tough one to see got a lot of respect for him, got a lot of love for him and I know he'll come back stronger."

Dart suffered the injury on New York's opening drive after two defenders sandwiched him on a pass attempt. Before exiting the contest, Dart completed 3 of 5 passes for 20 yards. While initial tests provided mild optimism, detailed MRI evaluations revealed damage to his MCL, PCL, and meniscus, forcing him to undergo season-ending surgery.

The Giants struggled without their rising leader under center, managing just two field goals as the offense stalled out. Meanwhile, Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns to anchor Los Angeles in the victory.

The bond between Daboll and Dart grew strong during their time together in East Rutherford, where Daboll placed immense trust in the young quarterback. L osing Dart certainly derails New York's immediate plans, but Daboll remains confident that the resilient quarterback possesses the mental toughness to return even stronger in 2027.

articles.title: ‘Leave My Garden King Alone’ — Kyle Juszczyk’s Wife Kristin Claps Back at NFL Over 49ers Star’s $14,926 Fine
articles.summary: The NFL’s crackdown on touchdown celebrations has claimed another player, but Kyle Juszczyk’s family isn’t exactly taking the league’s latest fine seriously....
articles.body:
The NFL's crackdown on touchdown celebrations has claimed another player, but Kyle Juszczyk 's family isn't exactly taking the league's latest fine seriously.

The league fined the San Francisco 49ers star $14,926 for what it called an "offensive demonstration" during the team's Week 2 win over the Miami Dolphins .

The league reportedly viewed Juszczyk's celebration as an imitation of chugging a beer and deemed the gesture inappropriate. There was just one problem: Juszczyk's nickname is "Juice," and he says he wasn't pretending to drink alcohol.

Kristin Juszczyk Turns NFL Fine Into an Orange Juice Joke

Juszczyk's wife, fashion designer Kristin Juszczyk, quickly responded to the fine on Instagram.

"His name is Juice. He's drinking Juice. He just has a broken finger, so he can't bend it… but he can still catch touchdowns," Kristin wrote on Instagram. "The irony of this is hilarious bc if you know Kyle, he barely drinks alcohol. Leave my garden King alone!"

Kristin even shared several Instagram stories showing Kyle and his friends recreating his signature juice-drinking celebration, noting that he's been doing it for years.

The couple later took the joke to TikTok, where they filmed themselves slicing and squeezing fresh oranges into a cup.

They captioned it, "A $14,926 glass of orange juice," taking a sly jab at the fine slapped on Juszczyk.

Kyle Juszczyk Explains His Touchdown Celebration

Juszczyk also addressed the fine while speaking to reporters in Santa Clara, explaining that the celebration honored his nickname.

"I don't know how else to say it: I wasn't drinking beer in my celebration," Juszczyk said . "I think you guys all know my nickname is 'Juice.' I have Juice on my pads. The stadium yells 'Juice' when I catch the ball."

He added that drinking juice has been part of his celebrations for years, which made the fine even more surprising.

Juszczyk even leaned into the controversy before meeting with reporters. He placed a beverage container on his locker shelf with "NOT BEER" written across it in bold marker. Next to it, he displayed a thigh pad with a juice-box design.

NFL Celebration Fines Extend Beyond Kyle Juszczyk

The NFL's decision comes amid a broader crackdown on celebrations the league considers inappropriate.

Detroit Lions star Amon-Ra St. Brown said the NFL fined him four times, at more than $14,000 per violation, following the game against the Buffalo Bills .

The NFL also fined Indianapolis Colts offensive lineman Matt Goncalves for a beverage-related gesture, and fined Cincinnati Bengals stars Ja'Marr Chase $29,852 and Tee Higgins $59,704 for multiple instances of their celebratory arm gesture.

Juszczyk has officially appealed his $14,926 fine, meaning the penalty remains under review.
